source.title: A class formula for admissible Anderson modules
source.authors: Bruno Anglès, Tuan Ngo Dac, Floric Tavares Ribeiro
source.version: HAL hal-02490566v2, deposited 16 September 2021; manuscript dated 22 June 2021; 31 numbered pages plus HAL cover. Not asserted identical to the 44-page version of record.
source.publicationComparison: Publisher landing page confirms authors, title, DOI, scope and 563–606 pagination, but exposes subscription preview only. Its acknowledgements mention corrections to an earlier manuscript. No identity of theorem wording, numbering or proof details with HAL v2 is claimed; journal collation is gap G1.

summary: The source proves a lattice-valued class formula [Lie_E(O_L):U_St(E/O_L)]_A=L(E/O_L) for admissible Anderson A-modules, proves admissibility from almost-everywhere principal deformed local Fitting ideals, and deduces the abelian, A-finite and arbitrary-coefficient Drinfeld cases. The existing DM.6 scope is the integral Drinfeld F_q[t] theorem; the general A, higher-dimensional and Stark-deformation branch needs a Part II. This is a substantive partial checkpoint: the preprint is read completely and its main theorem chain is decomposed, but journal collation, external higher-dimensional unit/motive inputs and several proof repairs remain explicit gaps, not formalized mathematics.

declarations.checked: Full statement and standing hypotheses read at f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369
declarations.provides: Finiteness of ClassGroup(R) for a Dedekind affine model R in an algebraic function field over a finite constant field.
ClassGroup R ≃* Pic R for every commutative domain.

conventions: q is a prime power; K/F_q is a one-variable global function field with F_q its full constants; infinity is a place of arbitrary degree d_infinity>=1; A is the Dedekind ring regular away from infinity, not assumed principal.
v_infinity has value group Z; the paper uses |x|=q^(-v_infinity(x)), so deg(aA)=-d_infinity*v_infinity(a), not -v_infinity(a).
F_infinity is the residue field of cardinality q^d_infinity. With a chosen uniformizer pi, K_infinity=F_infinity((pi)); for k=F_q(z), k_infinity=F_infinity(z)((pi)).
Atilde=F_q(z) tensor_F_q A and Ktilde_infinity is the Gauss completion of K_infinity(z). T_z(K_infinity) is the Gauss completion of K_infinity[z], not its z-adic completion; tau fixes z.

For an integral generic-characteristic E of dimension d>=1, iota:K->L is a finite extension, O_L the integral closure of iota(A), L_infinity=L tensor_K K_infinity; all Lie scalar structures use partial_E, including its nilpotent term.

[M':M] means determinant lattice of M divided by that of M'; for M subset M', it is Fitt(M'/M). It is an actual rank-one A-lattice in K_infinity, not a scalar modulo units or a chosen principal generator.

Within theorem statements below, 'integral E' abbreviates the preceding full generic-characteristic coefficient hypotheses; finite-field reduction statements explicitly replace the coefficient field. Definitions and conclusions never assume abelianity, A-finiteness or global surjectivity of exp unless stated.

A reported correction is a proposed repair to the pinned HAL v2, awaiting independent review and comparison with the version of record. In particular no assertion of a new error in the published article is made.

items.name: Function-field coefficient and completion datum
items.statement: Fix the coefficient datum in the conventions: A= {a in K: v_P(a)>=0 for P != infinity}, O_L is the integral closure in finite L/iota(K), and L_infinity=L tensor_K K_infinity. Infinity need not be rational, nor A principal.

api.name: FunctionFieldCoefficientData.regularAway
api.statement: Membership of a in A is equivalent to v_P(a)>=0 for every P other than infinity.

api.name: FunctionFieldCoefficientData.scalarTower
api.statement: The inclusions F_q -> A -> K -> L and their completed scalar maps form the specified commuting scalar towers.

api.name: FunctionFieldCoefficientData.infty_degree
api.statement: The residue degree d_infinity is positive and the residue field has cardinality q^d_infinity.

tests.name: FunctionFieldCoefficientData.test_rational_case

tests.name: FunctionFieldCoefficientData.test_constants_not_exact

tests.name: FunctionFieldCoefficientData.test_nonrational_place

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/2: Gauss coefficient extension and Tate algebra
uses.how: Extend v_infinity to K_infinity(z) by the minimum valuation of polynomial coefficients and subtraction on quotients. Its polynomial completion is T_z(K_infinity)=F_infinity[z]((pi)); its rational completion is Ktilde_infinity=F_infinity(z)((pi)). Put Atilde=F_q(z) tensor A, Otilde_L=F_q(z) tensor O_L, and T_z(L_infinity)=L_infinity tensor_K_infinity T_z(K_infinity).

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/10: Discrete full A-lattice
uses.how: For k=F_q or F_q(z), let R=k tensor A and V a finite-dimensional k_infinity-vector space, with its valuation topology. An R-lattice M subset V is an R-submodule which is discrete and spans V over k_infinity. No freeness is part of the definition.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/20: Anderson A-module in arbitrary coefficient ring
uses.how: For a field R over F_q with iota:A->R and d>=1, an Anderson A-module is an F_q-algebra homomorphism E:A->Mat_d(R){tau}, whose constant-term map partial_E satisfies (partial_E(a)-iota(a)I)^d=0 for all a, and whose image is not contained in Mat_d(R). An integral model means every coefficient lies in O_L. Drinfeld modules are the dimension-one case.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/61: Finiteness of the affine ideal class group
uses.how: For a Dedekind k-subalgebra R of an algebraic function field F/k with fraction field F and finite k, ClassGroup(R) is finite. Apply to A, after matching its affine-model structure.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/84: Perfect coefficient extension for motives
uses.how: Put F=L^perf and O_F the integral closure of A. Each prime P of O_L has a unique prime Q of O_F above it and O_L/P -> O_F/Q is an isomorphism. Define tau(x)=x^q and sigma(x)=x^(1/q) on F; on auxiliary z-extensions these maps fix z.

items.name: Gauss coefficient extension and Tate algebra
items.statement: Extend v_infinity to K_infinity(z) by the minimum valuation of polynomial coefficients and subtraction on quotients. Its polynomial completion is T_z(K_infinity)=F_infinity[z]((pi)); its rational completion is Ktilde_infinity=F_infinity(z)((pi)). Put Atilde=F_q(z) tensor A, Otilde_L=F_q(z) tensor O_L, and T_z(L_infinity)=L_infinity tensor_K_infinity T_z(K_infinity).

api.name: GaussCoefficientExtension.valuation_polynomial
api.statement: For nonzero sum a_i z^i the Gauss valuation is min_i v_infinity(a_i).

api.name: GaussCoefficientExtension.frobenius_z
api.statement: The coefficient Frobenius fixes z and has q-power action on K_infinity.

api.name: GaussCoefficientExtension.tate_to_field
api.statement: The inclusion of T_z(K_infinity) in Ktilde_infinity is isometric.

tests.name: GaussCoefficientExtension.test_norm_z
tests.statement: v_infinity(z)=0, hence z^n does not converge to zero in the Gauss topology.

tests.name: GaussCoefficientExtension.test_geometric_series
tests.statement: For v_infinity(pi)>0, sum_(n>=0) pi^n z^n belongs to T_z and equals (1-pi*z)^(-1).

tests.name: GaussCoefficientExtension.test_rational_not_tate

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/10: Discrete full A-lattice
uses.how: For k=F_q or F_q(z), let R=k tensor A and V a finite-dimensional k_infinity-vector space, with its valuation topology. An R-lattice M subset V is an R-submodule which is discrete and spans V over k_infinity. No freeness is part of the definition.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/28: z-deformation of an Anderson module
uses.how: If E_a=sum_i E_(a,i) tau^i, define Etilde_a=sum_i z^i E_(a,i) tau^i, with tau acting on coefficients by q-Frobenius and fixing z. Extend by F_q(z)-linearity to Atilde on Otilde_L-compatible modules. Specialization at z=1 gives E and at z=0 gives partial_E.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/30: Tate convergence of the deformed exponential
uses.how: exp_Etilde converges on T_z(L_infinity)^d and on Ltilde_infinity^d; on a sufficiently small ball it is an isometric bijection with inverse log_Etilde. Evaluation at z=1 intertwines exp_Etilde and exp_E.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/51: Admissibility and Euler convergence condition (C)
uses.how: With (P), require convergence to a nonzero element in Ktilde_infinity of product_(P notin S) x_P(0)/x_P(z). An integral Anderson A-module satisfying (P) and (C) is admissible. Convergence uses the infinity-adic Gauss valuation, not z-adic convergence.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/67: Finite-field cyclic scalar decomposition
uses.how: For F/F_q of degree m and V=F(z)^d, identify F(z) tensor_F_q(z) V with direct-sum_(j=0)^(m-1) V_j, where F acts on V_j by its q^j twist. Under psi(l tensor s)=(ls,l^q s,...,l^(q^(m-1))s), 1 tensor tau becomes the cyclic twisted shift sigma.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/78: Valuation bound on polynomial reciprocal roots
uses.how: Let F(z) in K_infinity[z], F(0)=1, deg F<r with r>=1, and v_infinity(F-1)>=C>=1 in the Gauss valuation. Factor F as product_(i=1)^r (1-alpha_i z), padding with zero alpha_i; then v_infinity(alpha_i)>=C/r, with v(0)=infinity.

items.name: Zeroth Fitting ideal
items.statement: For a finitely presented module M over a commutative ring R, choose R^a -> R^b -> M -> 0 and take the ideal of b by b minors; it is zero if a<b and the unit ideal for the zero module. The construction is independent of the presentation.

api.name: Module.fittingIdealZero.map

api.name: Module.fittingIdealZero.cyclic

tests.name: Module.fittingIdealZero.test_free_rank_one

tests.name: Module.fittingIdealZero.test_nonflat_image

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/4: Fitting ideal of a direct sum
uses.how: For finitely presented R-modules M,N, Fitt_0(M direct-sum N)=Fitt_0(M) Fitt_0(N).

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/5: Fitting and annihilator bounds
uses.how: For finitely presented M generated by b elements, Ann_R(M)^b subset Fitt_0(M) subset Ann_R(M).

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/6: Fitting submultiplicativity in exact sequences
uses.how: For a short exact sequence of finitely presented R-modules 0->M1->M->M2->0, Fitt_0(M1) Fitt_0(M2) subset Fitt_0(M).

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/7: Arbitrary base change of a Fitting ideal
uses.how: For a ring map f:R->S and finitely presented M, Fitt_0,S(S tensor_R M)=Ideal.map(f,Fitt_0,R(M)). In particular quotienting R by I gives the image ideal. Do not identify the image ideal with S tensor_R Fitt_0,R(M) without injectivity of its canonical map.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/8: Dedekind torsion-module elementary divisors
uses.how: For a Dedekind domain R and finitely generated torsion M, M is a finite direct sum of R/I_j for nonzero ideals I_j; Fitt_0(M)=product I_j. The ideals need not be principal.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/40: Local Fitting factor
uses.how: For a nonzero ideal I of O_L, Z_I(E/O_L)=Fitt_A(Lie_E(O_L/I)) Fitt_A(E(O_L/I))^(-1), as a fractional A-ideal inside K_infinity. Both modules are finite A-torsion modules.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/74: Residue-degree descent of the local Fitting ideal
uses.how: For finite F/F_q of degree m and any Anderson A-module E/F, there is an ideal I of A tensor_F_q F_q(z^m) such that Fitt_Atilde(Etilde(F(z)))=I Atilde. No principality is assumed here. The homogeneous-relation proof must use residue grading or Laurent localization, not the printed polynomial lower-bound condition in E10.

items.name: Fitting ideal of a direct sum
items.statement: For finitely presented R-modules M,N, Fitt_0(M direct-sum N)=Fitt_0(M) Fitt_0(N).
acceptance: For R=k[t], M=R/(t), N=R/(t^2), the product ideal is (t^3).

items.name: Fitting and annihilator bounds
items.statement: For finitely presented M generated by b elements, Ann_R(M)^b subset Fitt_0(M) subset Ann_R(M).
acceptance: For R=k[t], M=(R/(t))^2, Ann(M)=(t) while Fitt(M)=(t^2).

items.name: Fitting submultiplicativity in exact sequences
items.statement: For a short exact sequence of finitely presented R-modules 0->M1->M->M2->0, Fitt_0(M1) Fitt_0(M2) subset Fitt_0(M).
acceptance: For 0->R/(t)->R/(t^2)->R/(t)->0, the containment is equality (t^2).

items.name: Arbitrary base change of a Fitting ideal
items.statement: For a ring map f:R->S and finitely presented M, Fitt_0,S(S tensor_R M)=Ideal.map(f,Fitt_0,R(M)). In particular quotienting R by I gives the image ideal. Do not identify the image ideal with S tensor_R Fitt_0,R(M) without injectivity of its canonical map.
acceptance: Use the nonflat test R=k[x] -> k, M=R/(x): the image ideal is zero.

items.name: Dedekind torsion-module elementary divisors
items.statement: For a Dedekind domain R and finitely generated torsion M, M is a finite direct sum of R/I_j for nonzero ideals I_j; Fitt_0(M)=product I_j. The ideals need not be principal.
acceptance: For R a Dedekind domain with a nonprincipal prime P, do not require R/P to have a principal presentation ideal.

items.name: Exact Fitting multiplicativity over a Dedekind domain
items.statement: For a short exact sequence of finitely generated torsion modules over a Dedekind domain, Fitt(M)=Fitt(M1) Fitt(M2). Torsion and finite generation are retained.
acceptance: Local lengths at every nonzero prime add in the exact sequence and hence give equality of all ideal valuations.

items.name: Discrete full A-lattice
items.statement: For k=F_q or F_q(z), let R=k tensor A and V a finite-dimensional k_infinity-vector space, with its valuation topology. An R-lattice M subset V is an R-submodule which is discrete and spans V over k_infinity. No freeness is part of the definition.

api.name: DiscreteALattice.span_eq_top
api.statement: An R-lattice spans its ambient V over k_infinity.

api.name: DiscreteALattice.linearEquiv_map
api.statement: Continuous k_infinity-linear equivalences carry R-lattices to R-lattices and preserve identity/composition.

api.name: DiscreteALattice.finite_basis_quotient
api.statement: Full lattices have the equivalent finite-index basis description of item 12.

tests.name: DiscreteALattice.test_zero_space
tests.statement: The zero submodule is a full lattice in the zero vector space.

tests.name: DiscreteALattice.test_rational_standard
tests.statement: F_q[t]^n is a lattice in F_q((1/t))^n.

tests.name: DiscreteALattice.test_nondiscrete_span
tests.statement: For V=K_infinity nonzero, all of V as an A-submodule spans but is not discrete.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/11: Criterion for a discrete submodule
uses.how: An R-submodule M of V is discrete iff it contains an R-free submodule generated by a finite k_infinity-linearly independent family such that the quotient is finite-dimensional over k. The family need not span V.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/13: Rank-one lattice ratio
uses.how: For one-dimensional V, choose e !=0 and write M=alpha I e, M'=alpha' I' e with nonzero fractional R-ideals I,I'. Define [M':M]_R=(alpha/alpha') I (I')^(-1) inside k_infinity. Prove independence of e and the decompositions.

items.name: Criterion for a discrete submodule
items.statement: An R-submodule M of V is discrete iff it contains an R-free submodule generated by a finite k_infinity-linearly independent family such that the quotient is finite-dimensional over k. The family need not span V.
acceptance: The zero submodule is discrete with the empty independent family and zero quotient.

items.name: Three full-lattice criteria
items.statement: For n=dim_k_infinity V, M is an R-lattice iff it is discrete, finitely generated and of rank n; equivalently it contains the R-span of a k_infinity-basis with finite-dimensional k-quotient.
acceptance: A proper coordinate subspace lattice is discrete but fails the full-rank condition.

items.name: Rank-one lattice ratio
items.statement: For one-dimensional V, choose e !=0 and write M=alpha I e, M'=alpha' I' e with nonzero fractional R-ideals I,I'. Define [M':M]_R=(alpha/alpha') I (I')^(-1) inside k_infinity. Prove independence of e and the decompositions.

api.name: RankOneLattice.ratio.coordinate_formula
api.statement: For M=alpha I e and N=beta J e, [N:M]=(alpha/beta) I J^(-1).

api.name: RankOneLattice.ratio.basis_independent
api.statement: Replacing e by c e leaves the ratio unchanged.

api.name: RankOneLattice.ratio.scale
api.statement: [bN:aM]=(a/b)[N:M] for a,b nonzero in k_infinity.

tests.name: RankOneLattice.ratio.test_polynomial_index
tests.statement: For R=k[t], [R:tR]=tR.

tests.name: RankOneLattice.ratio.test_inverse_orientation
tests.statement: [tR:R]=t^(-1)R, not tR.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/14: Determinant lattice and general ratio
uses.how: For an R-lattice M in n-dimensional V, take the image of exteriorPower_R^n M in exteriorPower_k_infinity^n V. Define [M':M] by the rank-one ratio of these determinant lattices, with exterior degree zero interpreted as R inside k_infinity.

items.name: Determinant lattice and general ratio
items.statement: For an R-lattice M in n-dimensional V, take the image of exteriorPower_R^n M in exteriorPower_k_infinity^n V. Define [M':M] by the rank-one ratio of these determinant lattices, with exterior degree zero interpreted as R inside k_infinity.

api.name: ALattice.determinantRatio.topExteriorImage
api.statement: Map the top exterior power of the lattice into the top exterior power of V.

api.name: ALattice.determinantRatio.basis_formula
api.statement: Its coordinate ideal gives item 15's Steinitz formula without requiring freeness.

api.name: ALattice.determinantRatio.directSum
api.statement: The ratio for direct sums is the product of the individual ratios.

tests.name: ALattice.determinantRatio.test_rank_zero
tests.statement: Both zero-rank determinant lattices are R and their ratio is R.

tests.name: ALattice.determinantRatio.test_diagonal_index
tests.statement: For M=R^2 and N=tR direct-sum t^2R, [M:N]=t^3R.

tests.name: ALattice.determinantRatio.test_nonprincipal_rank_one
tests.statement: For a nonprincipal invertible ideal I, [R:I]=I; no scalar generator is chosen.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/15: Steinitz-coordinate ratio
uses.how: For n>=1 and decompositions M=R e1+...+R e_(n-1)+I e_n and M'=R f1+...+R f_(n-1)+J f_n, if sigma(e_i)=f_i, then [M':M]=det(sigma)^(-1) I J^(-1). The finite torsionfree/projective Steinitz decomposition is a required algebraic input, not a choice of free basis.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/16: Ratio inverse and cocycle laws
uses.how: For lattices M1,M2,M3 in the same V, [M1:M2]=[M2:M1]^(-1) and [M1:M3]=[M1:M2][M2:M3]; rank-one lattices in k_infinity form an abelian group.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/17: Index is the Fitting ideal
uses.how: If M' subset M are R-lattices in V, M/M' is finitely generated torsion and [M:M']=Fitt_R(M/M').

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/55: Projective lift of the identity modulo z^n
uses.how: Under item 54, use the projectivity of Lie_E(O_L) over A to choose an A-linear map mu:Lie_E(O_L)->B U_z with mu(m) congruent m modulo z^n. Extend to the rational completed Lie space; its determinant lies in 1+z^n B T_z(K_infinity).

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/56: Approximation of the regulator lattice
uses.how: Under the integrality of e_0,...,e_(n-1), every nonzero element x of [Lie_Etilde(Otilde_L):U_rat]_Atilde admits x=z^a(alpha+z^n beta), a in Z, alpha in B A not z-divisible and beta in B T_z(K_infinity). Expand each column with z^k, not z^j, and retain determinant cancellations below the first nonzero coefficient.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/62: Specialization of the regulator containment
uses.how: For admissible E, evaluate polynomial-unit lifts at z=1 and use their determinant ideals to obtain [Lie_E(O_L):U_St]_A subset L(E). No evaluation homomorphism on all of F_q(z) or Ktilde_infinity is used.

items.name: Steinitz-coordinate ratio
items.statement: For n>=1 and decompositions M=R e1+...+R e_(n-1)+I e_n and M'=R f1+...+R f_(n-1)+J f_n, if sigma(e_i)=f_i, then [M':M]=det(sigma)^(-1) I J^(-1). The finite torsionfree/projective Steinitz decomposition is a required algebraic input, not a choice of free basis.
acceptance: When n=1 the formula reduces to the rank-one ideal ratio, without assuming I or J principal.

items.name: Ratio inverse and cocycle laws
items.statement: For lattices M1,M2,M3 in the same V, [M1:M2]=[M2:M1]^(-1) and [M1:M3]=[M1:M2][M2:M3]; rank-one lattices in k_infinity form an abelian group.
acceptance: For R, tR and t^3R the ratios give t^3R=(tR)(t^2R) with the specified orientation.

items.name: Index is the Fitting ideal
items.statement: If M' subset M are R-lattices in V, M/M' is finitely generated torsion and [M:M']=Fitt_R(M/M').
acceptance: For M=R and M'=tR, both sides equal tR.

items.name: Determinant-index formula
items.statement: For a k_infinity-linear automorphism sigma of V and R-lattices with sigma(M) subset M', [M':M]=det(sigma)^(-1) Fitt_R(M'/sigma(M)).
acceptance: If sigma is multiplication by t and M=M'=R, det(sigma)^(-1)Fitt(R/tR)=R.

items.name: Positive Frobenius Ore algebra
items.statement: For an F_q-algebra R, construct matrices of additive skew polynomials with tau B=B^(q) tau and nonnegative tau powers. On perfect coefficient fields inverse twists may separately be defined; negative tau powers do not belong to this polynomial ring.
items.note: Generic SkewPolynomial is present, but the q-Frobenius action, matrix/additive-endomorphism comparison and this specialization remain planned.

api.name: FrobeniusSkewPolynomial.monomial_mul

api.name: FrobeniusSkewPolynomial.constantTerm

api.name: FrobeniusSkewPolynomial.eval_comp

tests.name: FrobeniusSkewPolynomial.test_constant_product

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/84: Perfect coefficient extension for motives
uses.how: Put F=L^perf and O_F the integral closure of A. Each prime P of O_L has a unique prime Q of O_F above it and O_L/P -> O_F/Q is an isomorphism. Define tau(x)=x^q and sigma(x)=x^(1/q) on F; on auxiliary z-extensions these maps fix z.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/91: Contravariant A-motive
uses.how: For E/F, take row vectors M(E/F)=F{tau}^(1 by d), with left F{tau}-action and right A-action m.a=m E_a, regarded as commuting left actions of A tensor F and tau. It is free of rank d over F{tau}, and (a tensor1-1 tensor iota(a))^d M subset tau M.

items.name: Anderson A-module in arbitrary coefficient ring
items.statement: For a field R over F_q with iota:A->R and d>=1, an Anderson A-module is an F_q-algebra homomorphism E:A->Mat_d(R){tau}, whose constant-term map partial_E satisfies (partial_E(a)-iota(a)I)^d=0 for all a, and whose image is not contained in Mat_d(R). An integral model means every coefficient lies in O_L. Drinfeld modules are the dimension-one case.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/23: Exponential and formal logarithm
uses.how: For integral E there are unique series exp_E=I+sum_(i>=1)e_i tau^i and log_E=I+sum_(i>=1)l_i tau^i with coefficients in Mat_d(L), satisfying exp_E partial_E(a)=E_a exp_E and log_E E_a=partial_E(a) log_E. They are two-sided inverses in the formal skew-series ring.

items.statement: Suppose e_i in Mat_d(O_L) for 0<=i<n. With B=F_q[z]_(z), every nonzero u in U_rat can be written z^a(alpha+z^n beta), where a in Z, alpha in B O_L[z]^d is not divisible by z and beta in B T_z(L_infinity)^d. Conversely each alpha in O_L^d lifts to alpha+z^n beta in B U_z.
acceptance: The leading coefficient cannot be removed when a is negative; rational z-units may have a pole at zero.

items.name: Projective lift of the identity modulo z^n
items.statement: Under item 54, use the projectivity of Lie_E(O_L) over A to choose an A-linear map mu:Lie_E(O_L)->B U_z with mu(m) congruent m modulo z^n. Extend to the rational completed Lie space; its determinant lies in 1+z^n B T_z(K_infinity).

api.statement: mu(m)-m belongs to z^n B T_z(L_infinity)^d.

api.statement: det(mu)-1 belongs to z^n B T_z(K_infinity).

tests.name: ALattice.projectiveApproximation.test_identity_case
tests.statement: When the identity map already lands in B U_z, it is a valid lift.

tests.name: ALattice.projectiveApproximation.test_det_first_order
tests.statement: For a two-dimensional mu=I+z^n C, det(mu)=1+z^n tr(C)+z^(2n)det(C).

tests.name: ALattice.projectiveApproximation.test_nonfree_lattice
tests.statement: The construction must work for a projective nonfree lattice; it cannot require a global A-basis.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/56: Approximation of the regulator lattice
uses.how: Under the integrality of e_0,...,e_(n-1), every nonzero element x of [Lie_Etilde(Otilde_L):U_rat]_Atilde admits x=z^a(alpha+z^n beta), a in Z, alpha in B A not z-divisible and beta in B T_z(K_infinity). Expand each column with z^k, not z^j, and retain determinant cancellations below the first nonzero coefficient.

items.name: Approximation of the regulator lattice
items.statement: Under the integrality of e_0,...,e_(n-1), every nonzero element x of [Lie_Etilde(Otilde_L):U_rat]_Atilde admits x=z^a(alpha+z^n beta), a in Z, alpha in B A not z-divisible and beta in B T_z(K_infinity). Expand each column with z^k, not z^j, and retain determinant cancellations below the first nonzero coefficient.
acceptance: A one-column constant vector must survive truncation; replacing z^k by z^j fails this test.

items.name: Exhausting sequence clearing exponential denominators
items.statement: Choose nonzero xi_n in O_L such that xi_n divides xi_(n+1), every nonzero prime contains some xi_n, and the first n coefficients of xi_n^(-1) exp_E xi_n are integral. Use finite prime sets in bounded residue degree and denominators of finitely many e_i.
items.locator: Theorem 4.3 proof Step 1, p. 17; corrected E6

api.statement: xi_n divides xi_(n+1).

api.name: AndersonAModule.denominatorSequence.prime_exhaustion

tests.name: AndersonAModule.denominatorSequence.test_nested_prime_sets

tests.name: AndersonAModule.denominatorSequence.test_reverse_impossible
tests.statement: If xi_(n+1) divides xi_n for all n, the prime support stays within that of xi_0 and cannot exhaust all primes.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/58: Regulator containment with principal local factors
uses.how: For admissible E with every Ztilde_P principal, [Lie_Etilde(Otilde_L):U_rat]_Atilde subset Ltilde(E). Apply item 56 to item 57's conjugates and pass to the Gauss limit in discrete A-coefficients. Uniform denominator control required for that passage is isolated as G3.

items.name: Regulator containment with principal local factors
items.statement: For admissible E with every Ztilde_P principal, [Lie_Etilde(Otilde_L):U_rat]_Atilde subset Ltilde(E). Apply item 56 to item 57's conjugates and pass to the Gauss limit in discrete A-coefficients. Uniform denominator control required for that passage is isolated as G3.
acceptance: Check that the prime supports of xi_n are increasing and the normalized local tail converges nonzero.

items.name: Deformed class-formula containment
items.statement: For every admissible integral E, [Lie_Etilde(Otilde_L):U_rat]_Atilde subset Ltilde(E). Remove the finite exceptional set by a nonzero scalar conjugation, apply the principal case and restore exactly the deformed local factors.
items.locator: Theorem 4.3 and proof Step 2, pp. 14, 17–18; E7
acceptance: A single exceptional prime is removed and then restored with its deformed, not z=1, factor.

items.name: Euler-characteristic valuation of regulator and class factor
items.statement: For any nonconstant t in A, regarding integral E as an Anderson F_q[t]-module, [Lie_E(O_L):U]_F_q[t] Fitt_F_q[t](H)=alpha_t F_q[t] for a nonzero alpha_t in F_q((1/t)) with v_infinity(alpha_t)=0; the same is [Lie_E(O_L):U_St]_F_q[t]. The generator is not asserted to lie in F_q[t].
items.locator: Lemma 4.6, p. 18, corrected E8; Taelman 2010 Theorem 2
acceptance: For q=2 Carlitz, zeta_A(1) is a nonconstant infinity-adic unit, not an element of F_2[t].

items.name: Finiteness of the affine ideal class group
items.statement: For a Dedekind k-subalgebra R of an algebraic function field F/k with fraction field F and finite k, ClassGroup(R) is finite. Apply to A, after matching its affine-model structure.
items.locator: Theorem 4.7 proof, p. 19; pinned affine-class-number theorem
items.note: Statement and standing hypotheses read in TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/RiemannRoch/AffineClassNumber.lean:70–109. No rational place or separability hypothesis is added.
acceptance: For the affine line over F_q, ClassGroup(F_q[t]) is the trivial finite group.

items.name: Specialization of the regulator containment
items.statement: For admissible E, evaluate polynomial-unit lifts at z=1 and use their determinant ideals to obtain [Lie_E(O_L):U_St]_A subset L(E). No evaluation homomorphism on all of F_q(z) or Ktilde_infinity is used.
acceptance: All chosen determinant entries have actual polynomial-unit lifts before evaluation; a pole at z=1 is inadmissible.

items.name: Class-group and norm upgrade from containment to equality
items.statement: In the principal-local-factor reduction of Theorem 4.7, write L(E)=uA with v_infinity(u)=0 and I=u^(-1)[Lie_E(O_L):U_St] subset A. Raise I to a principal power using finite ClassGroup(A), restrict the determinant index to F_q[t], and use the norm plus item 60 to show its principal generator has degree zero. Then I=A. Norm/restriction compatibility is an explicit input G4.
acceptance: An integral nonzero ideal of degree zero must be A; a proper prime ideal cannot pass this test.

items.name: Class formula for admissible Anderson A-modules
items.statement: For every admissible Anderson A-module E defined over O_L in the generic-characteristic setting, [Lie_E(O_L):U_St(E/O_L)]_A=L(E/O_L). Neither freeness of O_L nor rationality of infinity nor uniformizability of E is assumed.
acceptance: Specialize to A=F_q[t], d=1 to recover the old DM.6 formula through the explicit Stark quotient.

items.name: Ordinary-unit form of the class formula
items.statement: Under item 64's hypotheses, L(E/O_L)=[Lie_E(O_L):U(E/O_L)]_A Fitt_A(H(E/O_L)), by the Stark quotient formula and the index cocycle.
acceptance: Retain Fitt(H); setting it to A is permitted only when H=0.

items.name: Equality in the deformed class formula
items.statement: For admissible E, [Lie_Etilde(Otilde_L):U_rat]_Atilde=Ltilde(E). Remark 4.8 proposes the same argument over F_q(z); its Euler-characteristic and class-group inputs must be justified separately, not inferred from local compactness over a finite residue field.
acceptance: The rational deformed equality specializes only through regular Tate representatives, not a total F_q(z) evaluation.

items.name: Finite-field cyclic scalar decomposition
items.statement: For F/F_q of degree m and V=F(z)^d, identify F(z) tensor_F_q(z) V with direct-sum_(j=0)^(m-1) V_j, where F acts on V_j by its q^j twist. Under psi(l tensor s)=(ls,l^q s,...,l^(q^(m-1))s), 1 tensor tau becomes the cyclic twisted shift sigma.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/68: Characteristic polynomial of a deformed semilinear operator
uses.how: For r>=1 and A_i in Mat_d(F), put f=sum_(i=0)^r A_i z^i tau^i on F(z)^d, with tau fixing z, and chi(X,z)=det_F_q(z)(X I-f), a monic degree dm polynomial in X with coefficients in F_q[z].

uses.how: Under item 68, chi(X,z) belongs to F_q[X,z^m]. In each determinant monomial the total shift is zero modulo m; this also holds when the characteristic divides m.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/74: Residue-degree descent of the local Fitting ideal
uses.how: For finite F/F_q of degree m and any Anderson A-module E/F, there is an ideal I of A tensor_F_q F_q(z^m) such that Fitt_Atilde(Etilde(F(z)))=I Atilde. No principality is assumed here. The homogeneous-relation proof must use residue grading or Laurent localization, not the printed polynomial lower-bound condition in E10.

uses.where: PAPER-ANGLES-NGODAC-TAVARESRIBEIRO-22/95: Trace adjoint of a deformed finite-field action
uses.how: For F/F_q finite and Etilde_a=sum_(i>=0) z^i A_i tau^i on F(z)^d, equip F(z)^d with trace pairing <x,y>=Tr_F(z)/F_q(z)(x^T y). The adjoint action is Etilde_a^*=sum_(i>=0) z^i sigma^i(A_i^T) sigma^i, including i=0. In a basis with Gram matrix G its matrix is G^(-1)[Etilde_a]^T G, not necessarily the ordinary transpose in a normal basis.

No principality is assumed here. The homogeneous-relation proof must use residue grading or Laurent localization, not the printed polynomial lower-bound condition in E10.

items.name: Injection on Picard groups under rational constants
items.statement: The extension map Pic(A)->Pic(Atilde) is injective. The statement is about ideal classes; choosing a principal generator after extension does not yet supply good specializations at z=0 or 1.
acceptance: A nonprincipal ideal of A must not become principal solely by adjoining the rational constant z.

items.name: Torsion Picard classes under rational constants
items.statement: Via item 75, Pic(Atilde)_tors=Pic(A). The source's Jacobian argument is an external dependency G5: identify degree-zero divisor classes with Jacobian points, prove the required rational-function-field torsion assertion, and handle the degree d_infinity quotient.
acceptance: For A=F_q[t], both Picard groups in the asserted torsion comparison vanish.

items.name: Picard injection under z to z^m
items.statement: For m>=1, extension Pic(A tensor F_q(z^m))->Pic(Atilde) is injective. The norm first proves that a class in the kernel is torsion; descend that torsion class to Pic(A) and then use item 75. It does not immediately prove the ideal itself principal.
acceptance: When characteristic divides m, the norm still yields the mth power of the class; do not assume separability of z/z^m.

items.name: Valuation bound on polynomial reciprocal roots
items.statement: Let F(z) in K_infinity[z], F(0)=1, deg F<r with r>=1, and v_infinity(F-1)>=C>=1 in the Gauss valuation. Factor F as product_(i=1)^r (1-alpha_i z), padding with zero alpha_i; then v_infinity(alpha_i)>=C/r, with v(0)=infinity.
acceptance: For F=1+a z with v(a)>=C and any r>1, its one nonzero reciprocal root has valuation at least C/r.

items.statement: Condition (P') for integral E is: there exists a finite set S of nonzero primes of O_L such that Fitt_Atilde(Etilde(F_P(z))) is principal for every P outside S. Neither specialization generators nor convergence are assumed.

uses.how: For a fixed separating t and E_t=sum_(i=0)^r A_i tau^i, r>=1, the norm characteristic polynomial G_P(z)/G_P(0) has degree at most d*r in Y=z^m_P, with reciprocal roots of valuation at least m_P*(-v_infinity(t))/r. Norm-factor comparison bounds the roots of x_P(z)/x_P(0) similarly, hence these ratios tend to 1 and their product is a Tate-algebra unit. The weaker unweighted Lemma 5.5 estimate also suffices for convergence with a dimension-dependent constant.

items.name: Uniform root bound and Euler convergence from (P')
items.statement: For a fixed separating t and E_t=sum_(i=0)^r A_i tau^i, r>=1, the norm characteristic polynomial G_P(z)/G_P(0) has degree at most d*r in Y=z^m_P, with reciprocal roots of valuation at least m_P*(-v_infinity(t))/r. items.name: Specialization equality from ideal inclusions and degrees

routes.brief:
Build first on Drinfeld modules, t-motives and characteristic-p special values (DrinfeldModulesAndTModules), importing DM.0, DM.2, DM.4 and DM.6 only within their stated coefficient and uniformizability scope. Import Global function fields, reciprocity and automorphic foundations (FunctionFieldArithmetic) and the already built Tau Ceti AlgebraicCurves function-field/divisor/class-number APIs; import generic Fitting algebra from Integral Hecke actions, determinants and interpolation (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.6) and Steinitz/exterior determinant/norm transfer from Explicit K0: projectives, rank and determinant (KTheoryLowDegrees:Z.3–Z.4). Do not use retired FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration. Coordinate the polynomial-ring dual-motive special case with the previously extracted Ngo Dac 2021 multizeta branch; it is not a second owner of generic motive algebra.

Fix a global function field K with full constants F_q, an arbitrary place infinity of degree d_infinity>=1, A regular away from infinity, finite generic-characteristic L/K, O_L and L_infinity. Keep A Dedekind rather than principal. Construct topological A-lattices and their determinant ratios, Gauss/Tate and rational z-coefficient extensions, Anderson A-modules with nilpotent differentials, exponential and local logarithm, ordinary units/class modules, polynomial and rational z-units/classes, evaluation and Stark units. Prove the exact quotient/Fitting comparison, local factors, prime-power invariance and scalar-conjugation identities. Define admissibility by (P),(C), keeping exceptional ideals and convergence; prove the regulator containment, valuation normalization and norm/class-group upgrade. The first endpoint is Theorem 4.7: for every admissible integral E, [Lie_E(O_L):U_St(E/O_L)]_A=L(E/O_L), equivalently [Lie_E(O_L):U(E/O_L)]_A Fitt_A(H(E/O_L))=L(E/O_L).

Build the finite-field cyclic decomposition, graded characteristic-polynomial and weighted degree estimates, then the Fitting-ideal descent and Picard injection needed for Theorem 5.6: almost-everywhere principality of Fitt_Atilde(Etilde(F_P(z))) implies admissibility. Cover all Anderson F_q[t]-modules. Construct general-A motives and dual motives with their opposite Frobenius conventions; prove projectivity and almost-all preservation of abelianity/A-finiteness under reduction. Use corrected skew-motive cokernels and trace-pairing adjoints to prove Theorems 6.1 and 6.3. Deduce Theorem 6.4 for E abelian OR A-finite, and Corollary 6.5 for every integral Drinfeld A-module: L is a principal A-lattice and [O_L:U_St]_A=[O_L:U]_A Fitt_A(H)=L. Do not assume automatic analytic uniformizability or remove admissibility for arbitrary E.

Separate each listed definition and proof lemma, preserving the 40 definition contracts, nonflat-base-change, nonprincipal-lattice, Gauss-versus-z, nilpotent-differential, residue-degree and normal-basis tests. Complete G1–G8 before calling the design source-closed; compare the journal version and independently adjudicate E1–E14. Preserve full characteristic-p and bad-prime hypotheses. Later papers removing admissibility are outside this source's theorem scope. No Lean deliverable is authorized by this extraction issue.
